sentences.text:
Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Gajendra Singh

On The 4 th Of October, 2024
 Misc. Appeal No. 120 of 2019
 Ku. Sona Rathore
 Versus
 Naveen Kumar And Others
 Appearance:
 Ms. Abhilasha Jain - Adovocate for the appellant.
 Shri Sudarshan Pandit behalf of Shri Kushagra Singh -
 respondent No.3.
 Order

1. This misc. appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is preferred being aggrieved by the award dated 31.07.2018 in claim case No.20/2016 passed by M.A.C.T. Neemuch for enhancement of compensation of Rs.50,000/- .

2. As per para 32 & 35 of the impugned award the Tribunal has recorded the finding that victim Ku.
Sona sustained grievous injuries due to fracture of Femur bone but discarded the evidence of Dr.
O.P Gupta (AW-2) regarding permanent physical disability of 26% in right lower limb and 10% with regard to whole body vide Ex.P-33 on the ground that Sona was not earning and she is a student.

It is not proved that her earning capacity has been affected thereafter, Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.49,000/- (Rupees Forty Nine Thousand Only) in the following heads:-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:29080 2 MA-120-2019 (i) Medical Expenses 24,000/-
 (ii) Physical Pain 5,000/-
 (iii) Mental Pain 5,000/-
 (iv) Nutritious diet 5,000/-
 (v) Attendant, Travelling Expenses 5,000/-
 (vi) 01 month Loss of Education 5,000/-
 Total 49,000/-
3.
This misc. appeal has been preferred on the ground that Tribunal ought to have atleast assessed the notional income and awarded just compensation in pecuniary Ku.

sentences.text: 4. Counsel for the respondent has opposed the application.

Perused the record.
5. Perusal of MLC report (Ex.P/4), X-ray report (Ex.P/6), medical records (Ex.P/13) to (Ex.P/32)
and medical certificate (Ex.P/33) and loss of earning during treatment the amount has not been properly awarded.

This appeal is allowed and an amount of Rs.80,000/- (Rupees Eighty Thousand Only) is further enhanced in the heads of mental and physical pain with interest at the rate of 6%
from the date of application i.e 08.12.2024.
The other conditions of the award shall remain intact including the pay and cover.

6. The appellant has valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.50,000/- and paid the Court fee accordingly, however, for the remaining amount, the Court fee shall be paid by the appellant within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:29080 3 MA-120-2019 on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months,
the claimant shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
7. With the aforesaid this misc. appeal stands disposed of.
(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE akanksha Ku. Sona Rathore vs Naveen Kumar on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164834883/
